releases.notes:
## Pages of Atlas 0.4.2 — Minecraft 26.3

Pages of Atlas 0.4.2 is a correctness release for oversized resource packs on Minecraft 26.3. It preserves one logical atlas while safely splitting oversized block textures across as many as four physical GPU texture pages.

### Highlights

- Minecraft 26.3 and RenderPearl compatibility.
- GPU-safe virtual block-atlas paging with a 16384×16384 ceiling per physical page.
- A logical 32768×32768 atlas backed by up to four physical textures.
- Iris integration for paged diffuse, normal, and specular terrain textures.
- LabPBR normal/specular mapping, mipmaps, and parallax occlusion mapping support.
- Shader-independent sampler integration validated with Complementary Unbound and Photon.

### Fixed since 0.4.1

- Prevented large-GPU configurations from bypassing paging and attempting an unsafe monolithic 32768×32768 upload.
- Added explicit failure when an atlas requires more than four physical pages or when a paged upload cannot complete safely.
- Preserved authoritative sprite placement during page-anchor selection.
- Corrected Minecraft 26.3 2D texture allocation for neutral PBR fallback textures.
- Corrected neutral-normal channel encoding and LabPBR mip generation.
- Preserved gradient and explicit-LOD sampling for normal, specular, and POM shader paths.
- Restored Iris sampler units and RenderPearl physical texture-view attachment for all paged diffuse, normal, and specular samplers, including pipeline switches and reloads.
- Added regression tests for paging policy, allocation contracts, shader transformation, sampler registration, and actual `FrontendRenderPass` texture delivery.

### Validation

Runtime-tested on Minecraft 26.3 with Patrix 256×, all four diffuse pages, full normal/specular/POM rendering, shader switching, Complementary Unbound, and Photon. Automated paging and PBR verification suites also pass from a clean build.

### Known limits

- This artifact is for Minecraft 26.3 only.
- A logical block atlas is limited to four physical pages.
- High-resolution PBR pages require substantial VRAM, and initial synchronous page construction can cause temporary rendering stalls.
- Overflow-page animated PBR companions currently use their initial frame; animation advancement is not yet supported.

### SHA-256

```text
a9eeb661a205f4e41cb2b98792e8b5a60cc8ced7ad849e6d9f9753f6a0088b96  pagesofatlas-0.4.2-26.3.jar
```

The existing Minecraft 26.2 release is unchanged.

## Pages of Atlas 0.4.1 — Minecraft 26.3

This is a hotfix release for the Minecraft 26.3 build of Pages of Atlas.

### Fixed

- Fixed PBR physical-page uploads occurring while Sodium's externally owned terrain RenderPass was still active.
- Moved deferred PBR page construction to a RenderPearl-safe frame boundary before world rendering begins.
- Fixed custom item-cutout rendering by declaring the required default color target state.
- Fixed the RenderPearl color-attachment mismatch that could crash block/item rendering with high-resolution Patrix configurations.

### Validation

Validated on Minecraft 26.3 with:

- Patrix 26.3 resource packs
- Patrix Bonus Blocks
- Continuity
- Sodium
- Iris
- Photon with shaders enabled
- Shaders disabled
- Runtime resource reloads with F3+T

The Minecraft 26.2 build is not affected by this hotfix and remains at 0.4.0-26.2.

## Pages of Atlas 0.4.0 — Minecraft 26.3

0.4.0 is a major rendering architecture update. It replaces the previous direct multi-page block-atlas model with a production virtual-atlas system for oversized resource packs, and this build ports that architecture to Minecraft 26.3's new rendering stack.

### Virtual atlas architecture

- Added a fixed 32768×32768 logical block-atlas address space backed by four independently allocated physical atlas pages.
- Each physical page remains within the 16384×16384 GPU texture-size limit.
- Oversized block atlases automatically use the virtual-atlas renderer.
- Resource packs that fit on a single physical page continue to use Minecraft's normal single-atlas path.
- Added logical virtual sprites so Minecraft, Fabric Renderer API, Sodium, and Continuity can operate in one continuous sprite/UV space.
- Physical sprites remain responsible for actual GPU upload and page-local texture storage.
- Added generation-aware publication so a new atlas generation does not become active until its physical-page state is ready.

### Terrain and item rendering

- Added dedicated virtual-atlas terrain shaders.
- Terrain rendering now resolves physical-page ownership from logical atlas UVs and converts to page-local coordinates at render time.
- Added page-aware block-item rendering across vanilla/Fabric Renderer API, Indigo, and Sodium paths.
- Added page-aware Sodium extended block-model rendering, including item frames.
- Updated logical sprite lookup for Fabric Renderer API, Sodium, and Continuity.
- Preserved correct PBR normal/specular alignment with the corresponding diffuse page.
- Preserved page-local derivatives and mip selection after virtual-to-physical UV conversion.

### Shader compatibility

- Expanded Iris shader transformation support for virtual-atlas sampling.
- Fixed Photon POM coordinate routing through the virtual atlas.
- Fixed Solas compatibility for shader programs with different mid-texture-coordinate inputs.
- Validated with Photon/POM, Solas, Complementary / Unbound, and Shrimple.

### Minecraft 26.3 port

- Migrated GPU texture, render-pass, pipeline, and bind-group integration to RenderPearl.
- Added Minecraft 26.3 multidraw terrain support.
- Added 26.3 OIT/translucency pipeline support.
- Updated Sodium integration for 0.9.3-alpha.1.
- Updated Iris integration for 1.11.7.
- Updated Fabric Renderer API integration for Minecraft 26.3.
- Updated item rendering for the 26.3 vertex format, including UV3 forwarding.
- Removed the obsolete manual OpenGL sampler-unit remapping; RenderPearl now manages sampler bindings directly.

### Runtime validation

Validated with:

- Vanilla textures
- Patrix 128x
- Sodium
- Iris
- Continuity
- Item frames
- Runtime resource reloads
- Photon, including POM
- Solas
- Complementary / Unbound
- Shrimple

A high-resolution Patrix configuration produced a logical 32768×32768 block atlas containing 12,702 sprites while all physical textures remained within the 16384×16384 GPU limit.

### Requirements

- Minecraft 26.3
- Fabric Loader 0.19.3+
- Fabric API 0.161.0+
- Iris 1.11.7+
- Sodium 0.9.3-alpha.1+

Continuity is optional.

### SHA-256

`5289165259f29ac48cdb4b25c61e7e65f00063053d1ce42ee397a6cbc149ff21`

Compared with the previous v0.3.15 release, 0.4.0-26.3 changes 50 files with 3,674 insertions and 790 deletions.

## Pages of Atlas 0.4.0 — Minecraft 26.2

0.4.0 replaces the previous direct multi-page block-atlas rendering model with a production virtual-atlas architecture for oversized resource packs.

### Added

- Added a fixed 32768×32768 logical block-atlas address space backed by four independently allocated physical atlas pages, each capped at 16384×16384.
- Added automatic virtual-atlas activation when the block atlas requires more than one physical texture.
- Added logical virtual sprites so Minecraft, Fabric Renderer API, Sodium, and Continuity can operate in one continuous sprite/UV space while Pages of Atlas retains separate physical sprites for GPU upload.
- Added dedicated virtual-atlas terrain shaders for Minecraft and Sodium.
- Added page-aware item and block-model rendering for vanilla/Fabric Renderer API, Indigo, and Sodium rendering paths.
- Added page-aware Sodium extended block-model rendering used by item frames and other block-model feature renderers.
- Added generation-aware publication of virtual atlas plans and uploads.
- Added optional virtual-atlas diagnostics for page placement, physical-page routing, and UV conversion.

### Changed

- Reworked oversized block-atlas packing around one logical atlas instead of exposing physical pages directly to normal sprite lookup and rendering.
- Terrain now derives physical-page ownership from logical atlas UVs and converts those coordinates to page-local UVs at render time.
- Reworked block-item rendering to resolve the correct physical page per quad.
- Updated Fabric Renderer API and Indigo quad handling for logical-to-physical page translation.
- Updated Sodium sprite lookup and terrain rendering for the logical atlas.
- Updated Continuity CTM lookup to search the combined logical sprite space.
- Expanded Iris shader transformation support for virtual-atlas UV conversion, physical-page sampling, and PBR companion textures.
- Preserved normal/specular PBR page alignment with the corresponding diffuse physical page.
- Removed the previous proof-of-concept activation path; oversized block atlases now select the production virtual renderer automatically.
- Resource packs that fit on one physical page continue to use Minecraft's normal single-atlas path.

### Fixed

- Fixed item-frame and Sodium extended block-model rendering when a block texture resides on a secondary physical atlas page.
- Fixed logical sprite lookup for Fabric Renderer API, Sodium, and Continuity while retaining physical page-zero state required by upload and PBR code.
- Fixed page-local terrain sampling so implicit derivatives and mip selection remain correct after virtual-to-physical UV conversion.
- Fixed Photon POM coordinate routing through the virtual atlas.
- Fixed Solas compatibility for shader programs whose mid-texture-coordinate inputs differ from other Iris shader packs.

### Compatibility

Validated on Minecraft 26.2 with high-resolution Patrix resource packs, Sodium, Iris, Continuity, Photon, Solas, and Complementary / Unbound.

### Requirements

- Minecraft 26.2
- Fabric Loader 0.19.3+
- Fabric API 0.156.0+
- Iris 1.11.2+
- Sodium 0.9.1+

### SHA-256

## Fixes

- Fixes block-item textures on secondary physical atlas pages rendering gray in inventory and hotbar GUI slots.
- Aligns page-specific item pipelines with Minecraft 26.2's native item shader and complete diffuse, overlay, and lightmap sampler contract.
- Preserves per-quad physical-page routing for item models whose quads span multiple atlas pages.
